Apple Wallet in iOS 27 adds a handful of welcome new features, and today’s beta 2 brought another—Insights—to US users. Here are the details.

‘Insights’ is new in Apple Wallet with iOS 27, here’s what it does

Apple Wallet has long been the digital home for credit cards, debit cards, Apple Pay Cash, and other financial tools.

But in iOS 27, Apple is introducing a new feature designed to help you better track your money: Insights.

The feature was available in iOS 27 beta 1 in certain parts of the world, and today’s beta 2 release brings it the US for the first time.

Tap the three-dot icon in the top-right corner of Wallet to find Insights. Here’s how Apple describes it:

See Spending Insights and more


Connect accounts to Wallet to see spending insights, recurring transactions, account balances, and more.

Though I’m unable to see any of my own Insights just yet in the beta, my colleague Benjamin Mayo has had them in the UK since beta 1. Here’s a quick look:

Insights in Wallet may look familiar if you use Apple’s Health app. They strongly resemble some of the visualization features in Health that offer insights into your activity, sleep, and more.

Now in iOS 27, that same concept of organizing and visualizing your data is coming to Wallet and your spending.

With this new feature, data from the various payment accounts you have saved in Wallet will be aggregated to offer financial insights about trends, total spending, and more.

It’s an exciting addition that, combined with iOS 27’s other new Wallet features, makes Apple’s digital wallet more useful than ever.

Do you plan to use Insights in Apple Wallet? Let us know in the comments.
